moat_against: Niche-by-niche competition from larger, deeper rivals (Eaton, Parker Hannifin, Flowserve, TE Connectivity, ZF/Knorr-Bremse)
Cyclical end markets — auto production, industrial short-cycle, energy capex
SPX FLOW integration risk and post-deal leverage (~2.5x at Q2 2026) after the FY-end net-cash position was deployed
Equity raise for SPX FLOW lifted diluted shares from 79.9M (FY2025) to 88.4M (H1 2026 YTD) — historical buyback tailwind reversed
Commodity/steel and tariff cost exposure, only partly offset by pricing
moat_for: Spec-in, qualified components for harsh/critical applications — switching requires requalification
Installed-base aftermarket in pumps (Goulds) and flow products — recurring, higher-margin revenue
Leading niche brands: Goulds Pumps, ITT Cannon connectors, KONI, Friction Technologies
Demonstrated pricing power — price/cost favorable, adjusted operating margin guided to ~20.5% for 2026
Aerospace/defense backlog and multi-year program visibility in Connect & Control
moat_justification: Spec-in engineered components with installed-base aftermarket in pumps, qualified high-reliability aerospace/defense connectors, and leading friction/KONI brands support pricing power and ~20% adjusted operating margins, but positions are niche-by-niche against larger diversified rivals (Eaton, Parker Hannifin, Flowserve, TE Connectivity), end markets are cyclical, and the SPX FLOW deal adds integration and leverage risk.
name: ITT Inc.
one_liner: Quality engineered-components maker, moat 6/10 — does not clear 15% at $197.54 (weighted IRR 7.33%, weighted IV@15 $69.39); it clears 15% only at about $69, so the price pays for far more growth than the filing-based OE supports.
